Archive item 2: Evaluation Notebook – Dr. Amelia Tan
Source format: evaluation notebook

Note: GNC's outreach worker mentioned that many seniors who attend the centre also receive food deliveries from another org (Meals on Wheels). Potential double-counting in beneficiary numbers – need to clarify with GNC how they define "unique beneficiary".

---

**22 Aug 2019**

Comments on framework v1.1 received from 9 of 12 partners. Key themes:
- Need more guidance on what counts as a "successful referral" (e.g., does the beneficiary need to attend the first appointment?).
- Some partners want to report qualitative outcomes, not just numbers.
- Request for a simpler data collection template for small orgs.

Will address these in v1.2. Deadline for final framework: 30 Aug.

---

**29 Aug 2019**

Framework v1.2 finalised. Changes:
- Added definition: "successful referral" = beneficiary attends first appointment at the referred service.
- Added optional qualitative outcome section (max 1 page per quarter).
- Created two data collection templates: Standard (for orgs with >100 beneficiaries/yr) and Simplified (for smaller orgs).

Distributed to all partners. Training session scheduled for 12 Sep at CIF office.

---

**12 Sep 2019**

Training session held. 10 of 12 partners attended (2 sent apologies). Covered:
- How to use the data collection templates.
- Common mistakes in filling out the forms.
- Quarterly reporting deadlines (15 Jan, 15 Apr, 15 Jul, 15 Oct).

Feedback from session: partners want a sample filled-in form. Will create one using anonymised data from GNC's pilot.

---

**20 Sep 2019**

Created sample form using GNC pilot data (anonymised). Distributed via email. Also posted on CIF intranet.

---

**1 Oct 2019**

Quarterly reporting period #1 begins (Jul–Sep 2019). Reminder sent to all partners. Deadline: 15 Oct.

---

**15 Oct 2019**

Received reports from 8 of 12 partners by deadline. 3 more came in by 18 Oct. 1 partner (Bright Path Society) has not submitted – sent follow-up email. Will call if no response by end of week.

Dr. Amelia Tan role is listed as Program Evaluator in the evaluation notebook. Record status: current.

Initial review of reports: data quality is mixed. Some partners clearly used the simplified template, others tried the standard one and left many fields blank. Will compile summary for management.

---

**24 Oct 2019**

Bright Path Society submitted their report late (21 Oct). Reason: staff turnover – their M&E person left mid-September. New person is catching up. Will flag this in my notes for the mid-year review.

---

**31 Oct 2019**

Compiled Q3 2019 summary report. Key findings:
- 10 of 12 partners submitted on time.
- Total beneficiaries served: 3,847 (across all partners; some double-counting possible due to overlaps in service delivery).
- Most common outcome reported: "improved social connectedness" (mentioned by 7 partners).

Presented to CIF management on 5 Nov. They asked for more analysis on cost per beneficiary – will need to collect financial data in the next reporting round.

---

**12 Nov 2019**

Added cost-per-beneficiary question to the next quarterly report template. Partners will need to provide total programme expenditure and number of unique beneficiaries. Some partners may not track this – will need to provide guidance.

---

**20 Nov 2019**

Site visit #2: Health Access Initiative (HAI), Jurong. HAI runs a community health screening programme for low-income residents. Met with programme coordinator. They use a mobile app for data collection – much more advanced than most partners. They track:
- Number of screenings
- Referrals made
- Follow-up appointments attended

HAI's data is clean and well-organised. Could be a model for other partners. Will note this in my end-of-year summary.

---

**15 Jan 2020**

Q4 2019 reports due. Received 11 of 12 by 20 Jan. Bright Path Society submitted late again (23 Jan) – same reason: staff capacity. Will discuss with their director at the mid-year review.

---

**30 Jan 2020**

Compiled Q4 2019 summary. Total beneficiaries: 4,102 (slight increase from Q3). Cost-per-beneficiary data was patchy – only 5 partners provided full expenditure figures. Will need to improve this.
**16 Feb 2020**

Follow-up call with Bright Path Society. Their new M&E officer, Ms. Faridah, seems capable but is still learning the reporting cycle. She asked for a copy of the Q4 template – I sent it again. Will schedule a short training session with her before the Q1 2020 deadline.

---

**28 Feb 2020**

Site visit #3: Community Kitchen Collective (CKC), Bedok. They run a weekly meal delivery for elderly residents. Their record-keeping is mostly paper-based – they use a register book. The coordinator said they tried a tablet last year but it got stolen. Data is accurate but hard to aggregate. Suggested they use the simplified template at least.

---

**12 Mar 2020**

CIF management called a meeting about COVID-19. All site visits suspended until further notice. Partners are shifting to remote service delivery where possible. Need to adjust reporting expectations – some partners may not be able to collect data as usual. Will send guidance next week.

---

**25 Mar 2020**

Sent all partners a COVID-19 addendum: reporting deadlines extended by two weeks for Q1 2020. Also added a field for "remote vs in-person service delivery" in the template. Some partners may struggle with this – will monitor.

---

**10 Apr 2020**

Q1 2020 reports received. 9 of 12 on time (extended deadline). Bright Path Society submitted on time – good progress. CKC submitted late (paper records, no scanner at home). Data quality is mixed: some partners have gaps in beneficiary counts due to service interruptions.

---

**30 Apr 2020**

Compiled Q1 2020 summary. Total beneficiaries: 2,876 – significant drop from Q4 2019 (4,102). Expected due to COVID-19 restrictions. Remote delivery reported by 6 partners. Cost-per-beneficiary data still patchy – only 4 partners provided full figures. Will flag this trend in the mid-year report.

---

**15 May 2020**

Webinar for partners on remote data collection. 8 of 12 attended. HAI shared their mobile app approach – several partners expressed interest. Will follow up with a resource pack.

---

**20 May 2020**

CIF management asked for a special COVID-19 impact assessment. Will need to collect qualitative data from partners on service delivery changes, client needs, and staff capacity. Drafting a short survey – will send by end of month.

---

**10 Jun 2020**

COVID-19 impact survey sent to all partners. 12 responses received by 30 Jun. Key themes:
- Increased demand for food assistance
- Difficulty reaching elderly clients without digital access
- Staff burnout and volunteer shortages

Will compile a full report for management by mid-July.

---

**15 Jul 2020**

Submitted COVID-19 impact report to CIF management. They requested a follow-up on two partners with significant service disruptions: UHC and Bright Path Society. Will schedule phone calls with both.

---

**20 Jul 2020**

Phone call with United Health Collective (UHC). Their community clinic services were suspended for two months (April–May). They resumed limited in-person consultations in June. Their data for Q1 and Q2 2020 is incomplete – they could not track all interactions during the suspension. Will work with them on a catch-up plan.

---

**05 Aug 2020**

Q2 2020 reports due. Received 10 of 12 by 10 Aug. UHC submitted late (14 Aug) with partial data – missing beneficiary counts for April and May. Their coordinator said the suspension disrupted their tracking system. Will discuss at the mid-year review.

---

**28 Aug 2020**

Mid-year review meeting with all partners (virtual). Key discussion points:
- Data quality during COVID-19
- Remote delivery challenges
- Reporting burden – some partners asked for a simpler template

Will consider a simplified template for the next reporting round.

---

**15 Sep 2020**

Drafted a simplified quarterly report template – fewer fields, more focus on outcomes. Will pilot with three partners (including UHC) in Q3 2020. HAI will continue with the standard template.

---

**30 Sep 2020**

Q3 2020 reports due. Pilot partners used the simplified template – feedback was positive. UHC submitted on time with complete data – good improvement. Other partners used the standard template; data quality is improving.

documents.title: Evaluation Notebook – Dr. Amelia Tan
documents.content:
Note: GNC's outreach worker mentioned that many seniors who attend the centre also receive food deliveries from another org (Meals on Wheels). Potential double-counting in beneficiary numbers – need to clarify with GNC how they define "unique beneficiary".

---

**22 Aug 2019**

Comments on framework v1.1 received from 9 of 12 partners. Key themes:
- Need more guidance on what counts as a "successful referral" (e.g., does the beneficiary need to attend the first appointment?).
- Some partners want to report qualitative outcomes, not just numbers.
- Request for a simpler data collection template for small orgs.

Will address these in v1.2. Deadline for final framework: 30 Aug.

---

**29 Aug 2019**

Framework v1.2 finalised. Changes:
- Added definition: "successful referral" = beneficiary attends first appointment at the referred service.
- Added optional qualitative outcome section (max 1 page per quarter).
- Created two data collection templates: Standard (for orgs with >100 beneficiaries/yr) and Simplified (for smaller orgs).

Distributed to all partners. Training session scheduled for 12 Sep at CIF office.

---

**12 Sep 2019**

Training session held. 10 of 12 partners attended (2 sent apologies). Covered:
- How to use the data collection templates.
- Common mistakes in filling out the forms.
- Quarterly reporting deadlines (15 Jan, 15 Apr, 15 Jul, 15 Oct).

Feedback from session: partners want a sample filled-in form. Will create one using anonymised data from GNC's pilot.

---

**20 Sep 2019**

Created sample form using GNC pilot data (anonymised). Distributed via email. Also posted on CIF intranet.

---

**1 Oct 2019**

Quarterly reporting period #1 begins (Jul–Sep 2019). Reminder sent to all partners. Deadline: 15 Oct.

---

**15 Oct 2019**

Received reports from 8 of 12 partners by deadline. 3 more came in by 18 Oct. 1 partner (Bright Path Society) has not submitted – sent follow-up email. Will call if no response by end of week.

Dr. Amelia Tan role is listed as Program Evaluator in the evaluation notebook. Record status: current.

Initial review of reports: data quality is mixed. Some partners clearly used the simplified template, others tried the standard one and left many fields blank. Will compile summary for management.

---

**24 Oct 2019**

Bright Path Society submitted their report late (21 Oct). Reason: staff turnover – their M&E person left mid-September. New person is catching up. Will flag this in my notes for the mid-year review.

---

**31 Oct 2019**

Compiled Q3 2019 summary report. Key findings:
- 10 of 12 partners submitted on time.
- Total beneficiaries served: 3,847 (across all partners; some double-counting possible due to overlaps in service delivery).
- Most common outcome reported: "improved social connectedness" (mentioned by 7 partners).

Presented to CIF management on 5 Nov. They asked for more analysis on cost per beneficiary – will need to collect financial data in the next reporting round.

---

**12 Nov 2019**

Added cost-per-beneficiary question to the next quarterly report template. Partners will need to provide total programme expenditure and number of unique beneficiaries. Some partners may not track this – will need to provide guidance.

---

**20 Nov 2019**

Site visit #2: Health Access Initiative (HAI), Jurong. HAI runs a community health screening programme for low-income residents. Met with programme coordinator. They use a mobile app for data collection – much more advanced than most partners. They track:
- Number of screenings
- Referrals made
- Follow-up appointments attended

HAI's data is clean and well-organised. Could be a model for other partners. Will note this in my end-of-year summary.

---

**15 Jan 2020**

Q4 2019 reports due. Received 11 of 12 by 20 Jan. Bright Path Society submitted late again (23 Jan) – same reason: staff capacity. Will discuss with their director at the mid-year review.

---

**30 Jan 2020**

Compiled Q4 2019 summary. Total beneficiaries: 4,102 (slight increase from Q3). Cost-per-beneficiary data was patchy – only 5 partners provided full expenditure figures. Will need to improve this.

documents.title: Evaluation Notebook – Dr. Amelia Tan
documents.content:
**16 Feb 2020**

Follow-up call with Bright Path Society. Their new M&E officer, Ms. Faridah, seems capable but is still learning the reporting cycle. She asked for a copy of the Q4 template – I sent it again. Will schedule a short training session with her before the Q1 2020 deadline.

---

**28 Feb 2020**

Site visit #3: Community Kitchen Collective (CKC), Bedok. They run a weekly meal delivery for elderly residents. Their record-keeping is mostly paper-based – they use a register book. The coordinator said they tried a tablet last year but it got stolen. Data is accurate but hard to aggregate. Suggested they use the simplified template at least.

---

**12 Mar 2020**

CIF management called a meeting about COVID-19. All site visits suspended until further notice. Partners are shifting to remote service delivery where possible. Need to adjust reporting expectations – some partners may not be able to collect data as usual. Will send guidance next week.

---

**25 Mar 2020**

Sent all partners a COVID-19 addendum: reporting deadlines extended by two weeks for Q1 2020. Also added a field for "remote vs in-person service delivery" in the template. Some partners may struggle with this – will monitor.

---

**10 Apr 2020**

Q1 2020 reports received. 9 of 12 on time (extended deadline). Bright Path Society submitted on time – good progress. CKC submitted late (paper records, no scanner at home). Data quality is mixed: some partners have gaps in beneficiary counts due to service interruptions.

---

**30 Apr 2020**

Compiled Q1 2020 summary. Total beneficiaries: 2,876 – significant drop from Q4 2019 (4,102). Expected due to COVID-19 restrictions. Remote delivery reported by 6 partners. Cost-per-beneficiary data still patchy – only 4 partners provided full figures. Will flag this trend in the mid-year report.

---

**15 May 2020**

Webinar for partners on remote data collection. 8 of 12 attended. HAI shared their mobile app approach – several partners expressed interest. Will follow up with a resource pack.

---

**20 May 2020**

CIF management asked for a special COVID-19 impact assessment. Will need to collect qualitative data from partners on service delivery changes, client needs, and staff capacity. Drafting a short survey – will send by end of month.

---

**10 Jun 2020**

COVID-19 impact survey sent to all partners. 12 responses received by 30 Jun. Key themes:
- Increased demand for food assistance
- Difficulty reaching elderly clients without digital access
- Staff burnout and volunteer shortages

Will compile a full report for management by mid-July.

---

**15 Jul 2020**

Submitted COVID-19 impact report to CIF management. They requested a follow-up on two partners with significant service disruptions: UHC and Bright Path Society. Will schedule phone calls with both.

---

**20 Jul 2020**

Phone call with United Health Collective (UHC). Their community clinic services were suspended for two months (April–May). They resumed limited in-person consultations in June. Their data for Q1 and Q2 2020 is incomplete – they could not track all interactions during the suspension. Will work with them on a catch-up plan.

---

**05 Aug 2020**

Q2 2020 reports due. Received 10 of 12 by 10 Aug. UHC submitted late (14 Aug) with partial data – missing beneficiary counts for April and May. Their coordinator said the suspension disrupted their tracking system. Will discuss at the mid-year review.

---

**28 Aug 2020**

Mid-year review meeting with all partners (virtual). Key discussion points:
- Data quality during COVID-19
- Remote delivery challenges
- Reporting burden – some partners asked for a simpler template

Will consider a simplified template for the next reporting round.

---

**15 Sep 2020**

Drafted a simplified quarterly report template – fewer fields, more focus on outcomes. Will pilot with three partners (including UHC) in Q3 2020. HAI will continue with the standard template.

---

**30 Sep 2020**

Q3 2020 reports due. Pilot partners used the simplified template – feedback was positive. UHC submitted on time with complete data – good improvement. Other partners used the standard template; data quality is improving.
